claims.statement: JFrog documents a MyJFrog API token, generated by a Primary Admin in the MyJFrog portal, used to authenticate calls to the MyJFrog API, expiring after one year.

sources.supports: "API tokens allow you to make changes to your JFrog account via REST API"; "The API token expires after one year."
sources.locator: sections "Use an API Token in MyJFrog" and "Create an API Token in MyJFrog"

claims.statement: JFrog's MyJFrog Portal API reference documents authentication as an access token sent as a bearer token in the Authorization header (Authorization: Bearer <token>), and states that only a Primary Admin can generate MyJFrog tokens.

sources.supports: Access Tokens as bearer token in authorization header (Authorization: Bearer <token>)
sources.locator: MyJFrog Portal API reference (OpenAPI info.description), Authentication

sources.supports: Access Token as bearer token (Only a Primary Admin can generate MyJFrog tokens)
sources.locator: MyJFrog Portal API reference (OpenAPI securitySchemes, BearerAuth)

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Candidate established at existence level only; format, variants, benign siblings and lifecycle are not researched.
The page states no prefix, length or alphabet, and does not say whether the MyJFrog API token is a JWT or an access token of the Platform.

The MyJFrog API reference calls the credential an Access Token and the MyJFrog page calls it an API token; whether it is the same kind of token as a JFrog Platform access token is not stated, and it stays a separate family.
